ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus himalayicus* reaches 70 mm SVL. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal bands and a pale nuchal collar. Key features include strongly curved digits and a lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus himalayicus* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 5–7 dark, irregular transverse bands that are narrower than the pale interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus himalayicus* inhabits moist temperate forests in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalaya Bent-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and invertebrates across rocky surfaces and forest terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus himalayicus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus himalayicus* is found in the Himalayan foothills of West Bengal and Sikkim, India, typically inhabiting elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
